payload.query: Need contrast-enhanced chest CT, chest MRI, FDG PET-CT, and histopathological biopsy results for the right thoracic mass. These are missing core items to confirm neoplastic nature, intratumoral vascularity, local invasion, and metastasis, thereby verifying or excluding the leading hypothesis of right intrathoracic tumor.
payload.retrieval_output: Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) scan of the chest showed a large, heterogeneous mass measuring 20.8 cm × 13.6 cm × 13 cm in size in the right hemithorax. The mass was broad based toward the pleura and compressing medially onto the right lung, leading to its compressive atelectasis. However, there was no invasion of the collapsed lung, which was showing a uniform, homogeneous enhancement. The chest wall muscles also showed normal attenuation, and no erosion or lytic destruction of the ribs was seen. The mass was predominantly hypodense with an average attenuation of 10 Hounsfield units (HUs). There were small peripheral fat attenuation areas (−70–−90 HU) and few calcific foci (+650–+900 HU) within the mass. An USG-guided biopsy was performed, which showed predominantly myxoid tissue with scattered atypical cells and lipoblasts in a myxoid background. Immunohistochemistry revealed that the tumor cells were positive for S100, whereas the stroma stained well with Alcian blue, suggesting an abundant mucinous background.

payload.report: Two months of chest pain and dyspnea with right hemithoracic dullness suggested a right thoracic process. Imaging showed a 20.8×13.6×13 cm heterogeneous pleural-based mass with fat/calcification and atelectasis. Biopsy revealed myxoid tissue, atypical cells, lipoblasts, S100 positivity and Alcian blue-positive mucin; the pathologist favors myxoid liposarcoma, the gold standard for tumor nature, refuting empyema and primary lung disease. Molecular, PET/MRI and LDH data are lacking, leaving subtype, grade and staging unconfirmed.
